Which defines IPv6-only as the state of an operational system or service when IPv4 protocol functions (addressing, packet forwarding) are not in use. The NIST USGv6 profile defines technical requirements for a product to be capable of operating in IPv6-Only environments. IPv6-Only technology, in accordance with the USGv6 Program (https://www.nist.gov/programs-projects/usgv6-program/usgv6-revision-1), NIST Special Publication (SP) 500-267B Revision 1 “USGv6 Profile” (https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.SP.500-267Br1), and NIST SP 800-119 “Guidelines for

As part of this transition, the VA must preserve, manage, and provide compliant access to hundreds of millions of legacy call recordings currently stored across three on-premise platforms: Calabrio One, Avaya, and Verint. These recordings must be retained in accordance with National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) mandates, with variable retention policies by call type — including crisis, benefits, and healthcare interactions. The VA needs a solution that extracts, decrypts, and standardizes its legacy recordings into an open format, consolidates them into a single compliant archive, and allows the decommissioning of these platforms once the contact center migration is complete. As part of this transition, the VA must preserve, manage, and provide compliant access to hundreds of millions of legacy call recordings currently stored across three on-premise platforms: Calabrio One, Avaya, and Verint. These recordings must be retained in accordance with National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) mandates, with variable retention policies by call type — including crisis, benefits, and healthcare interactions. The VA needs a solution that extracts, decrypts, and standardizes its legacy recordings into an open format, consolidates them into a single compliant archive, and allows the decommissioning of these platforms once the contact center migration is complete. ITEM 1 SALIENT CHARACTERISTICS 1.11 Source Systems The VA's legacy recording environment consists of the following systems: Calabrio One v11.5 (Main Production) — Single-tenant, Azure Cloud storage. Confirmed file count: approximately 227,381,000 files (January 2018 – present). Calab

Continuity Replay. Continuity Replay shall be configured at deployment to enforce NARA retention requirements across the VA's diverse call types. The system shall apply retention periods based on metadata attributes — such as call type, department, or location — ensuring that crisis calls, benefits interactions, and healthcare recordings are each held for the appropriate duration and automatically purged upon expiry. Legal hold capabilities will allow the VA to pause purge on specific files flagged for audit, compliance review, or litigation support. Core Capabilities Dashboard: Real-time visibility into interactions under legal hold, files scheduled for purge in the next 30 days, and total archive metrics by year. Advanced Search & Replay: Intuitive filter interface by date range, user, interaction ID, group, department, call type, and custom tags. Playback of any archived audio directly in-browser. On-Demand Transcription: Any archived call can be transcribed within the platform, regardless of whether it was transcribed by the original recording system. Useful for the VA's ad hoc transcription workflows. NARA Retention Engine: Configurable retention policies by metadata attribute. Automatic purge scheduling with pre-purge notification. Legal hold to override purge for specific interactions. Role-Based Access Control (RBAC): Granular permissions by user, group, or department.

The FASTPASS program seeks to prevent contaminated or substandard medications from reaching patients by developing a system, comprised of multiple technologies, to perform rapid, non-contact drug quality and safety testing at points of entry and across the supply chain. American patients deserve to know that the drugs they take meet the quality and eﬃcacy standards that the FDA approved. FDA inspections are still the gold standard for quality assurance, ensuring that U.S. medical products are safe and eﬀective. However, United States depends heavily and increasingly on global pharmaceutical supply chains for key starting materials, active pharmaceutical ingredients, and ﬁnished drug products. As this dependence has grown, the challenge of ensuring the quality and safety of imported pharmaceuticals has grown with it. Existing oversight tools—including facility inspections and laboratory-based testing remain essential— but are stretched thin supporting the magnitude and complexity of today’s international supply chains. If a protest is filed externally, the agency protest will be dismissed. ===== FILE: files/Attachment_2_SOW_1232SA26Q1199.pdf ===== Statement of Work Enterprise Facility Infrastructure Engineering and Operations Support for BARC, BHNRC, and USNA During BARC Transition and Closure 1.0 Background Personnel and operational activities at the U.S. National Arboretum (USNA) are increasing as functions are relocated from the Beltsville Agricultural Research Center (BARC), creating greater demand on shared network, compute, storage, database, monitoring, cybersecurity, and facility-supporting infrastructure. At the same time, BARC research programs, scientific data, applications, and supporting systems are being transferred to receiving locations throughout the United States, requiring the existing infrastructure to remain secure, reliable, and continuously available throughout the migration process. The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Agricultural Research Service (ARS) relies on BARC, the Beltsville Human Nutrition Research Center (BHNRC), and USNA to conduct mission-critical research and support laboratory operations, facility systems, environmental monitoring, cybersecuri

ring, cybersecurity, and facility-supporting infrastructure. At the same time, BARC research programs, scientific data, applications, and supporting systems are being transferred to receiving locations throughout the United States, requiring the existing infrastructure to remain secure, reliable, and continuously available throughout the migration process. The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Agricultural Research Service (ARS) relies on BARC, the Beltsville Human Nutrition Research Center (BHNRC), and USNA to conduct mission-critical research and support laboratory operations, facility systems, environmental monitoring, cybersecurity, and administrative functions. These locations operate through an interconnected enterprise infrastructure that provides shared services essential to daily Government operations. USDA requires enterprise infrastructure operations and engineering support to sustain mission-critical IT services across BARC, BHNRC, and USNA during the ongoing BARC transition and phased closure. The contractor must support current operations while enabling the orderly migration of research workloads, scientific data, applications, and associated systems to their receiving locations. Scope of Work The contractor shall perform archival digitization services for historical audiovisual media, including but not limited to: (85) 16mm picture film (silent and sound, where applicable) (44) VHS videocassettes (55) Betamax videocassettes (18) U-Matic (2) other Ampex and 1” Total estimated time in minutes – 5485 minutes Services shall include inspection, cleaning (when appropriate), stabilization, digitization, quality control, documentation, and return of all original materials. 3. Film Archivist Requirement A qualified Film Archivist or training learned under a film archivist shall be physically present on-site throughout all handling, inspection, preparation, and digitization activities. The Film Archivist shall possess: A minimum of five (3) years of professional experience in audiovisual archival preservation and digitization. Demonstrated experience handling historical, rare, fragile, deteriorating, or unique audiovisual collections. Knowledge of archival standards and best practices for film and magnetic media preservation. Experience identifying film shrinkage, vinegar syndrome, mold, tape degradation, binder hydrolysis, and other preservation concerns. Authority to halt digitization if media conditions present a risk of damage until appropri

requirements. 10. Government-Furnished Property The Government shall provide the historical audiovisual materials to be digitized and identify any known special handling requirements. 11. Acceptance Criteria The project shall be considered complete when: All media have been digitized. All required metadata have been delivered. Quality control has been completed. Original media have been returned without damage. All deliverables have been accepted by the project lead 12. Period of Performance The period of performance shall be 180 days from the date of award. Work shall be coordinated with the Government to minimize disruption and ensure the availability of the Film Archivist during all digitization activities. ===== FILE: files/Statement_of_Work_-_Historical_Film_Digitization_28002_29_unpacked/[Content_Types].xml ===== <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes"?> <Types xmlns="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/package/2006/content-types"><Default Extension="rels" ContentType="application/vnd.openxmlformats-package.relationships+xml"/><Default Extension="xml" ContentType="application/xml"/><Override PartName="/word/document.xml" ContentType="application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document.main+xml"/><Override PartName="/word/numbering.xml" ContentType="app

deliverables_scope.text: . There are several projects and applications throughout NESDIS that will be migrating into NCCF. A procurement of the Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe) Enterprise Subscription (SES) Licenses will support the training approach for use of agile practices and the guidance on execution of several initiatives including the continued development of NCCF and the migrations of applications, algorithms development, and product generation within NCCF. Also, a procurement will enable continued progression towards accomplishment of the NESDIS Transformation Strategic Objective to develop agile, scalable ground capability to improve efficiency of service deliverables and ingest data from all sources. Transitioning from SES products would require significant investment by the Government across several program offices to facilitate and result in a substantial duplication of cost to the Government that is not expected to be recovered through competition. Thus, not procuring the SES renewal would present an unacceptable impact to the Government. No other product will meet the Government’s Requirements. New UPS panelboards will be added to allow for redundant receptacles for all the mission equipment within the High-Altitude Electromagnetic Pulse (HEMP)-shielded equipment room. Emergency Power Off (EPO) will be upgraded to the latest MDA GMD standards. Power Control and Monitoring System (PCMS) and Power Quality Monitoring System (PQMS) will also be extended into IDT1 from the Fort Greely Power Plant (FPP).The estimated dollar magnitude of this project is anticipated between $1,000,000 and $5,000,000. The primary objective of this market research is to understand the breadth of vendor capability to provide the full catalog of DISA PA’d CSOs. DISA is exploring multiple acquisition strategies to ensure 100% catalog coverage, robust competition, and administrative efficiency. The Government is also assessing the viability of various socioeconomic set-aside strategies and seeks to understand the market depth at all business sizes. An additional, a critical operational challenge this vehicle aims to solve is the translation of high-level mission requirements (e.g., the Government needs a data analytics capability for 100 users at Impact Level (IL) 5) into specific orderable Bills of Material (BOMs). United States person as deﬁned in 26 U.S.C. 7701(a)(30) means (1) A citizen or resident of the United States; (2) A domestic partnership; (3) A domestic corporation; (4) Any estate (other than a foreign estate, within the meaning of 26 U.S.C. 701(a)(31)); and (5) Any trust if- (i) A court within the United States is able to exercise primary supervision over the administration of the trust; and (ii) One or more United States persons have the authority to control all substantial decisions of the trust. Background: The U.S. Army Formation Based Layered Protection Experimentation Division (FBLP ExDIV) is a critical asset in the Army and the Department of Defense for simulations and analysis in support of U.S. Army Maneuver Support Center of Excellence and Chemical, Engineer, and Military Police Corps issues. The FBLP ExDIV supports the Army Vision, the Army Modeling and Simulation Master Plan, and Army Transformation efforts by conducting experimentation and analysis to assess warfighting concepts, design forces, determine requirements, and evaluate Doctrine, Organizations, Training, Materiel, Leadership and Education, Personnel, and Facilities (DOTMLPF) concepts and programs for the Maneuver Support Center of Excellence (MSCoE). Gathering data to underpin analysis to inform decision makers at all levels is the primary task of the FBLP ExDIV and the primary avenue for generating that data for analysis is through computer-based experimentation and studies. 1.3.
